correctness.rationale: Explicit stage times have both dominant active-one and dominant reset blocks. The single-prototype upper estimate holds at every n by the pointwise one-hot inequality and exact Wasserstein distance to a Dirac. At the end of a dominating active block one orbit tends to the all-one Dirac and the other k−1 orbits tend to the all-zero Dirac; the triangle inequality yields a lower error bound 1/k for every possible single prototype, giving the exact strict threshold. The number of symbolic transitions up to n is o(n), so each empirical trajectory approaches mixtures of the two constant Dirac measures; its cluster set is the entire line segment. For any N common prototypes, a radius-r ball intersects this length-one Wasserstein geodesic in diameter <=2r; midpoint prototypes attain minimax radius exactly 1/(2N). Strict < epsilon produces floor(1/(2epsilon))+1. No numerical or finite-enumeration lemma is relied upon.
